Checked all five steps, F1–F4, and all three exact-sequence cases on an arbitrary ringed space. Finite generators admit simultaneous local lifts through a sheaf epimorphism. Projection of ker epsilon surjects onto ker gamma (choose the negative of a lift under delta); images of finite-type sheaves have finite local generators. In the extension case injectivity of i identifies ker delta with the preimage needed to generate ker g. Zero modules and rank-zero free maps satisfy the same arguments. The exact-sequence diagram has correct orientation. Demailly II3.13–3.14 supplies the general ringed-space argument; Wehler Release 5.0 Propositions 4.32/4.34 and Release 4.3 Propositions 4.31/4.33 agree. Citation edition ambiguity amended; no mathematical interface change.

Checked all four steps and F1–F6. For q=1 the integral-domain argument gives zero. If P_q(x) is a unit, the elementary relations generate with degree at most d. Otherwise translation to (x_prime,w_0) makes P_q regular of order r between 1 and e. Preparation and uniqueness of division show the unit u is a polynomial of degree e-r. Subtracting (t_j/u)(P_q e_j-P_j e_q) leaves remainders of degree below r; multiplying the residual vector by u gives component degrees at most d-1. Division uniqueness forces its last component to be polynomial. This proves the bound at every point, not only at the center. n=1 uses constant base coefficients. Compared with Demailly II3.20 complete proof and Wehler 4.28(iii.2–iii.3); the local proof correctly retains units even where source notation suppresses them. Common-center clarification accepted; the only direct item consumer is the owned Oka theorem, whose preparation step supplies these hypotheses. Checked every one of the 12 steps and all 17 cited dependency statements. The supplier definition uses positive complex dimension; C^0 is the auxiliary induction base. Empty tuples, zero germs and unit entries are handled before simultaneous preparation of the nonzero product. The coefficient matrix has q(d+1) columns and 2d+1 rows. A polynomial relation germ at (x_prime,w_0) gives a base coefficient relation because a polynomial vanishing on a product neighborhood has zero coefficients; translation between w and w-w_0 preserves the degree bound. Dimension induction plus the matrix lemma gives one neighborhood generating K. The Noetherian stalk and coherent-cokernel argument in steps 6–7 is valid though more than is needed. Extending coefficient sections to the product and using bounded-degree reduction generates all relation stalks. Free modules are coherent by the matrix lemma; finite repeated coherent kernels give the requested partial resolution, including ell=0, with no left-end exactness claim. AC is retained as adopted ambient scope, not inferred necessary. Demailly II3.19–3.20 and II3.17, and Wehler 4.28, checked. No missing prerequisite or empirical premise.

Cancellation in the holomorphic germ domain then gives (a,b)=c(-z_2,z_1). Stalkwise equality proves generation of the sheaf on D, without claiming arbitrary global coefficients from stalk data. Oka plus the split extension makes the free source coherent; kernel calculus gives coherence. Inherited AC is explicit; no measurements or global resolution are asserted.
